A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeFoG. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-generation experiments, sampling and training ablations, runtime measurements, and conditional digital-pathology results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds RRWP feature-control experiments, including Table 11 and Figure 19.

M1.justification: The core noising process, transformer, loss, and CTMC sampling formulation are retained. However, v1's optional exact-expectation optimization and its settings disappear, while v2 still defines rates through expectations. The PDFs do not establish whether the computation changed or only its description and reporting were removed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Planar, Tree, SBM, QM9 with implicit and explicit hydrogens, MOSES, Guacamol, and conditional low/high TLS generation. The added feature controls use retained datasets and tasks; moving TLS results into the appendix does not remove coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 7, and 8 add GruM and CatFlow comparisons on Planar, SBM, and QM9. Table 11 and Figure 19 introduce DiGress with RRWP as a feature-matched comparator. DiGress also joins previously reported molecular sampling-efficiency comparisons, substantially strengthening the comparator coverage.

E3.justification: Table 8 adds charge-aware relaxed validity alongside standard QM9 validity. The RRWP study introduces controlled feature substitutions and sampling-step comparisons. The hyperparameter-table caption also corrects the reversed molecular/synthetic sampling budgets to 500/1000 steps; this does not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 expands the feature-runtime analysis into a controlled study of RRWP's effects on generation quality and sampling efficiency across three datasets (Table 11, Figure 19). Conversely, exact-expectation ablation curves disappear from the cumulative optimization plots. Main-text Figure 3 reorganizes existing Planar sweeps rather than introducing a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-sampling-run reporting and the same mean-plus-standard-deviation practice. No changed run counts, seed disclosures, confidence-interval methods, or significance tests are documented. Added result rows follow existing reporting practices.

E6.justification: New comparator, relaxed-validity, and RRWP-control results substantially expand the evidence, while exact-expectation curves are removed. Added GruM achieves QM9 FCD 0.11 versus DeFoG's retained 0.12, changing the ranking. Table 8 also changes DiGress's uniqueness deviation from 0.2 to 0.1. Headline DeFoG benchmark means remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit graph-specific Corollaries 1–2 and proofs that distinguish node and edge alphabets. The general rate-estimation and distribution-error theorems and Assumption 6 are retained. The permutation-invariance proof additionally makes its use of the invariant initial distribution explicit.

C1.justification: The central discrete-flow, training–sampling decoupling, and state-of-the-art generation claims remain. The efficiency claim is strengthened from performance comparable to certain diffusion models with 5–10% of their steps in v1's introduction to outperforming most diffusion models with that fraction in v2's abstract.

C2.justification: Appendix G.4 newly interprets the RRWP controls as evidence that framework decoupling drives the principal gains. Section 5.3 adds more specific interpretations of guidance and stochasticity at different step budgets. The conclusion refocuses future work on sampling optimization, fewer steps, and larger graphs.

D1.justification: v2 removes the Exact Exp settings column: v1 Table 6 specifies true for Planar and false elsewhere, whereas v2 Table 5 no longer discloses these choices. Hardware, runtime measurements, remaining hyperparameters, and the code-repository disclosure are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands research positioning through comparator descriptions and detailed distinctions between continuous/discrete state spaces, time formulations, and training–sampling coupling. v2 adds CatFlow's variational-flow work and further sampling references, explicitly distinguishing DeFoG from another flow-based graph generator.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, framework exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves later, graph-specific corollaries enter the framework section, and architecture details and TLS experiments move into appendices. A dedicated main-text ablation section changes the narrative organization.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two columns. Figure 1 gains a conceptual positioning panel, existing Planar analyses are recomposed into Figure 3, and Table 11/Figure 19 add feature-control displays. Tables gain or reorder columns, while numerous figures and tables are resized, restyled, or relocated.

improvement.justification: The RRWP controls, broader comparator set, separate relaxed-validity reporting, and explicit graph-specific proofs improve attribution, comparability, and clarity. These gains are tempered by lost exact-expectation settings and an unrevised QM9 FCD-superiority claim despite the added GruM result of 0.11 versus DeFoG's 0.12. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
